newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares end firmer as Telecom bounces off lows.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares end firmer as Telecom bounces off lows.

text.p: * NZ shares end firmer, buoyed by 14 cent rise in Telecom
* Fletcher Building firms despite going ex 6.5 cent div
* Volume boosted by portfolio
Price movements at close
LAST CHG
316 nil * NZSC cap index -8.65 at 5,051.23
349 +1 * Volume NZ$61.3 million. June futures untraded
643 +14 * Other movers - +13 +18
New Zealand shares closed firmer on Monday, buoyed by a rebound in Telecom and strength in Fletcher Building.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index gained 12.23 points to close at 2,238.84, with Telecom up 14 cents to NZ$6.43 and FCL Building up 13 at $4.45.
Several stocks went ex dividend, including all of the Fletcher stocks, which brokers said was the equivalent of a 7.8 point deficit for the index.
"So in actual fact the market's up about 20 points," said Craig Robins at County Natwest.
FCL Building's gain was despite a 6.5 cent dividend. Brokers said the stock had been sold down too aggressively last month after reporting a fall in half-year profit.

"I think the market over-reacted to the result and we're now back up to more realistic levels," said Robins. "It's still a good company with a very good outlook, exposed to the growth parts of the economy."

Another strong performer on the day was gas explorer Cultus Petroleum. It continued to race higher on the back of a promising outlook for its exploration programme, rising 23 cents to a new high of $3.35.
But brokers said the market overall still lacked any real direction and was wary of further volatility in the Dow.

"The market really doesn't feel as if it's going anywhere. It's still really looking for direction from offshore -- you can see how jittery it gets whenever Wall Street has a bad day," said Robins. -- Matthew Brockett (64 4) 471 4275
